title: mistri check --json
description: What `mistri check --json` prints, and what the `check` tool of `mistri observe --mcp` answers: every step's verdict and every finding of every step. Codes and fields are the contract; messages are sentences for a person and may change. The exit code is the command's: 0 passed, 1 could not check, 2 schema types, 3 typecheck, 4 validation, 5 components, 6 pending, 7 deploy.

version.description: This document's shape; a change to it is a new version.

app.description: The App checked, or null when it did not load far enough to say.

dir.description: The App directory, from where the command ran.

ok.description: Every step passed or was skipped; warnings and info never make it false.

exit.description: The exit code: the first step that failed.

routes.description: With --routes: every address the App answers to, and what it opens.

code.description: Stable: tsc's own code for a typecheck error (TS2322), a design rule's for a design warning, and otherwise one of the codes check-codes lists (unknown-column, unknown-action, query-grammar, role-cannot-read, …).

severity.description: An error fails its step; a warning and info never do.

file.description: Where it was written, from where the command ran.

path.description: Where in the App definition, where it can be told: views.tasks.query, resources.task.actions.close.when, pages.order[0].primary.

fix.description: What to change, where the check knows it.

promise.description: The theme contract's promise the code holds, C1 (text readable) to C13 (same App), on a theme-contrast, theme-edge, theme-focus, theme-chart, theme-dark, theme-budget or theme-print finding; mistri explain C2 says it.

docs.description: The page that explains the code.
